topic: Cosmides & Tooby (1989): Why Humans Flunk Abstract Logic (20%) Yet Catch Free-Riders Instantly (75%)!
visual_mode_reason: Leda Cosmides's landmark 1989 Cognition experiments (with John Tooby) — proving the exact same Wason 4-card puzzle that stumps 80% of Stanford students in abstract 'If P then Q' form jumps to 75% accuracy ONLY when framed as catching a 'Benefit Taken Without Paying the Cost' cheater (even on unfamiliar Cassava-Root/Tattoo rules!) — links dramatic 4-card tabletop flips directly to ventromedial prefrontal / amygdala social-exchange circuitry (confirmed in Patient R.M., Stone et al. 2002!).

primary_case.title: Leda Cosmides's 1989 Stanford / Harvard 'Logic of Social Exchange' Cassava-Root Cheater-Detection Experiments
primary_case.place: Stanford University & Harvard University (published in Cognition, 1989)

core_facts.fact: Remember **Peter Wason's 4-Card Logic Trap** (*'If a card has a vowel on one side, it has an even number on the other'* — Cards **E, K, 4, 7**)? Fewer than **10–25% of university students** turn over **E and 7 (P and not-Q)** — yet when Griggs & Cox (1982) changed it to **'If a person is drinking beer, they must be over 21'**, **~75%** nailed **Beer + 16-Year-Old**.

Skeptics said: *'Nothing special about cheating. People just know American drinking laws from real-world memory!'* So in **1989 (*Cognition*)**, **Leda Cosmides** designed a **brilliant 100%-unfamiliar test** nobody in America had ever experienced: **'If a man eats cassava root, then he must have a tattoo on his face'** — Cards: **Eats Cassava Root | Eats Molo Nuts | Tattoo | No Tattoo**.
Look at how Cosmides held the **exact 14-word rule and 4 cards 100% IDENTICAL** while changing ONLY the background story.

In the **Descriptive Folklore Story** (tattooed married men happen to live near cassava groves, so eating cassava correlates with having a tattoo), Stanford students scored down around **21–25%** — flunking just like abstract vowels and numbers.

In the **Social Contract Story** (cassava root is a prized, scarce delicacy rationed ONLY to men who endured the painful initiation ritual of getting a facial tattoo!), **75% of Stanford students INSTANTLY flipped 'Eats Cassava Root' + 'No Tattoo'** — catching the guy eating the prized root without paying the price.

Then Cosmides ran the **ULTIMATE killer experiment against formal logic (Switched Social Contract, Experiments 3 & 4, SRC1)**: *'If a man **pays the cost** (has a facial tattoo), then the tribe **must give him cassava root**'* — mathematically, formal logic *modus tollens* says flip **P & not-Q**. Instead, **~71% of humans flipped NOT-P ('No Tattoo') and Q ('Eats Cassava Root')** — VIOLATING formal propositional logic to catch the **Benefit-Without-Cost Cheater**.

Thirteen years later (**Stone, Cosmides, Tooby, Kroll & Knight, 2002 *PNAS***), bilateral **ventromedial/orbitofrontal + amygdala** injury patient **R.M.** provided stunning neurological double-dissociation: R.M. scored **70% normal** on identically structured **Safety/Precaution 4-card rules** (*'If you work with toxic TB patients, you must wear a surgical mask'*), yet plunged to **39% impaired** specifically on **Social-Contract Cheater rules**.

Balanced scientific debate (**Cheng & Holyoak 'Pragmatic Permission Schemas'; Sperber & Girotti relevance critique; Corning SRC3**): critics argue general **deontic permission/obligation rules** and conversational relevance contribute alongside evolutionary social-exchange pressures — yet everyone agrees **human reasoning rockets from ~20% to ~75% the moment an abstract rule becomes 'Who took the benefit without paying the cost?'**.

In Cosmides's (1989) social-exchange experiments, roughly 75–80% of participants failed abstract descriptive Wason rules yet jumped to ~75% logical violation detection on unfamiliar 'cassava root and facial tattoo' social contracts.

wow_facts.fact: Same 4 cards (**Eats Cassava | Eats Molo Nuts | Tattoo | No Tattoo**), same 0% prior American familiarity: frame it as a neutral geography fact and **75%+ fail**; frame Cassava as a **rationed Benefit earned by paying a Cost** and **75% solve it in seconds**.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Familiarity didn't solve the puzzle — flipping on the 'Free-Rider Radar' solved it.

wow_facts.fact: In Cosmides's **Switched Social Contract**, formal textbook logic demands flipping **P and not-Q** — yet **71% of smart adults flip NOT-P and Q instead**, breaking textbook logic to catch **'Took Benefit + Paid Zero Cost'**.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Proof positive that human minds run Social-Exchange logic, NOT Aristotle's truth tables.

wow_facts.fact: Neurological **Patient R.M.** (limbic orbitofrontal + amygdala damage) aced 4-card **Safety Hazard** puzzles ('Exposed to Hazard without Protection' = 70%) while selectively failing 4-card **Social Cheater** puzzles (39%).
wow_facts.why_surprising: Brain injury separated 'Watch out for danger!' from 'Watch out for freeloaders!' despite identical card logic.

misconceptions.myth: People only solve the Drinking-Age 4-card puzzle because they've visited bars and seen ID checks in real life.
misconceptions.truth: Cosmides's unfamiliar *Cassava Root & Facial Tattoo* rule (SRC1) had zero prior real-world memory in California — yet jumped from ~23% to 75% purely by framing it as Benefit-for-Cost.

misconceptions.myth: Humans are obsessed with catching ALL rule-breakers equally — including generous altruists who pay the cost and skip the reward.
misconceptions.truth: Cosmides tested **'Altruist Detection'** (paid the cost, didn't take cassava!) — people rarely flip those cards. Our radar locks specifically onto **Took the Benefit + Dodged the Cost**.

misconceptions.myth: To teach complex policies or contracts, write them in neutral abstract 'If Condition A, then Requirement B' prose.
misconceptions.truth: Abstract prose drops human accuracy near 20% — rewriting policies clearly in **'To receive Benefit X, you must complete Requirement Y'** triples comprehension.

everyday_hooks: Glazing over completely while reading an abstract software license or tax form — yet spotting within **0.4 seconds** when one coworker takes shared project credit after skipping every weekend shift.
Rewriting confusing team SOPs or customer policies into crisp **Benefit to Required Step** format so people stop making 80% errors.
Checking your own blind spot: because your brain hunts *other* people's unpaid benefits at 75% accuracy, pause to audit whether YOU quietly undercounted a teammate's contribution.
